      <div class="resource-card">
        <h3>Overview</h3>
        <p class="resource-description">
          This repository contains a simplified 2D model of the golf swing, focusing on planar motion analysis. 
          The reduced dimensionality makes it ideal for understanding core biomechanical principles, control-affine 
          dynamics, and drift-input decomposition without the complexity of full 3D simulations.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h3>Features</h3>
        <p class="resource-description">

          <strong>Fast Computation:</strong> Reduced computational requirements compared to 3D models<br>
          <strong>Educational Value:</strong> Ideal for learning fundamental biomechanical principles<br>
          <strong>Control Analysis:</strong> Tools for analyzing control-affine system properties<br>
          <strong>Visualization:</strong> 2D visualization tools for swing analysis
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h3>Use Cases</h3>
        <p class="resource-description">
          The 2D model is particularly useful for educational purposes, rapid prototyping of control strategies, 
          understanding fundamental dynamics before moving to 3D models, and scenarios where planar motion is 
          sufficient for analysis.
        </p>
